feedback: Format is compliant (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION), FINAL_STATES lists declared state u0, guards are predicate-only, the kill transition correctly excludes steps where a kill coincides with a breach (so no double-fire), plant_trampled is properly ignored as irrelevant to this task via the (u0, else) self-loop, and the +0.1 kill progress reward is bounded and aligned. However, the machine fails semantic fidelity for 'Try not to let zombies through any lane' because u1 is a bare absorbing sink: (u1, else) -> u1 is the only outgoing transition, so after the FIRST breach every subsequent top_breach and side_breach goes unpenalized and every zombie_killed goes unrewarded for the rest of the episode. The evidence shows breaches recur within single episodes (the example trace has side_breaches at steps 238, 256, 275, 293, and spawn chance rises to 17% late in the episode), so the task is a repeated soft constraint, not a one-shot failure: as written the RM collapses 'avoid breaches on any lane' to 'avoid exactly one breach'. Worst of all, a late top_breach after an earlier side_breach carries zero penalty, inverting the task's priority on the protected lane, and the kill shaping disappears exactly in the busy end-game where the agent most needs it (up to ~260 dead steps with no learning signal). To fix: either make breach penalties per-occurrence (breach self-loop on u0 with a negative reward) and keep the kill reward there, or keep the u1 violation sink for FINAL_STATES/acceptance purposes but give it real dynamics, e.g. (u1, top_breach | side_breach) -> u1 with the breach penalty and (u1, zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach) -> u1 with the kill reward, so ongoing violations and kills stay visible while u0 remains the only accepting state (no breach ever). Also consider whether a per-occurrence penalty of smaller magnitude (e.g. -1 to -5, possibly scaled so a top breach outweighs a side breach) is safer than a single -100 that must do all the work in one shot.

(u1, top_breach | side_breach) -> u1
(u1, zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach) -> u1
(u1, else) -> u1
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach | side_breach, u1) -> -10
(u0, zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach, u0) -> 0.1
(u1, top_breach | side_breach, u1) -> -5
(u1, zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach, u1) -> 0.1
feedback: Faithful and well-formed for 'Try not to let zombies through any lane'. FINAL_STATES is present and nonempty; u0 is declared in STATES and is genuinely accepting for this task: the episode is truncated at 300 steps, and ending in u0 means no zombie got through any lane, exactly the task's success condition. Semantic fidelity: both breach kinds are penalized (the task spans all lanes), kills are rewarded, and plant_trampled is correctly irrelevant, falling into the per-state else self-loops. Ordered coverage and determinism: the kill guard carries !top_breach & !side_breach, which is necessary here because a kill can coincide with a same-step breach (the agent kills on one lane while another zombie steps through elsewhere); with that negation each state's guards are mutually exclusive and else is their complement, so every possible label combination (kill+breach, trample+breach, both breach kinds on one step) maps to exactly one transition per state. Event semantics: all four propositions are step-transient events, and the else self-loops correctly handle empty steps, so there is no persistent/event confusion. Reward safety: no positive reward for any bad event; the first breach costs -10 and each subsequent breach costs -5 via the u1 self-loop, so every breach is counted; the +0.1 kill reward is bounded by the ~18-37 spawn cap (max ~3.7 total); totals are bounded over 300 steps. No regression is required: nothing in the domain un-breaches a lane, so the absorbing u1 with continued -5 penalties is the right structure for a soft 'try not to' task. Reachability and compactness are fine: u1 is reachable from u0 via any breach, and two states are minimal for the differentiated first-breach penalty. Minor nits, none blocking: (1) the else self-loop transitions have no explicit REWARD_FUNCTION entries and so imply 0 - if the harness demands a total reward function, add '(u0, else, u0) -> 0' and '(u1, else, u1) -> 0'; (2) when two zombies breach different lanes on the same step the boolean propositions yield a single penalty - a limitation of the proposition set, not of this machine; (3) the small kill reward relative to breach penalties correctly prioritizes lane defense over kill farming, which suits the task.
